subject: ela
intro: Each question gives you a short passage, stanza, or scene. Read it carefully, then choose the answer that best explains how that part fits into the structure of the whole text and how it develops the plot, setting, or theme. Pick the single best answer.

items.prompt:
Read the opening paragraph of a story.

Maya had lived in the same quiet town her whole life. Every morning she walked the same three blocks to school, waved to the same baker, and sat in the same seat by the window. Nothing ever changed, and Maya liked it that way.

What does this opening paragraph mainly do for the story as a whole?
A) It resolves the main conflict of the story.
B) It introduces the setting and Maya's ordinary world before anything changes.
C) It marks the climax, the highest point of tension in the story.
D) It reveals the lesson the story wants readers to learn.
items.answer: B) It introduces the setting and Maya's ordinary world before anything changes.

steps: An opening paragraph usually establishes the setting and the main character's normal life so that later changes stand out.
This paragraph describes Maya's quiet town and her unchanging routine, which is exactly the job of setting up the ordinary world.
B is correct because it names that structural job.
A is wrong because nothing has been resolved; the story has barely begun and no conflict has appeared yet.
C is wrong because there is no tension here; the climax comes near the end after a conflict builds.
D is wrong because the paragraph describes a scene, it does not state a lesson or theme.
solution.answer: B) It introduces the setting and Maya's ordinary world before anything changes.

items.prompt:
Read this short scene from near the end of a story.

With the rope finally tied tight, Devon climbed the last few feet and pulled himself onto the cliff top. The storm was gone. Below him the valley spread out, calm and green. He had made it. He sat down to rest and smiled.

Where does this moment most likely fall in the structure of the story?
A) The introduction, where characters are first introduced.
B) The rising action, where the trouble is just beginning.
C) The resolution, where the problem is solved and tension eases.
D) The climax, the moment of greatest danger.
items.answer: C) The resolution, where the problem is solved and tension eases.

steps: The resolution comes after the climax, when the main problem has been solved and the tension drops.
Devon has finished the dangerous climb, the storm is gone, the valley is calm, and he rests and smiles, all signs that the trouble is over.
C is correct because these clues show the conflict has eased.
A is wrong because characters and setting are not being introduced; the action is ending.
B is wrong because the trouble is not beginning, it is finishing.
D is wrong because the greatest danger has already passed; the storm is gone and Devon is safe.
solution.answer: C) The resolution, where the problem is solved and tension eases.

items.prompt:
Read this opening stanza of a poem.

The morning light slips through the trees,
A golden hush, a gentle breeze.
The garden wakes, the flowers rise,
And dew still clings beneath the skies.

What does this first stanza mainly do for the poem?
A) It establishes the setting and a calm, peaceful mood.
B) It states the main conflict the speaker must solve.
C) It marks the turning point of the poem.
D) It resolves a problem introduced earlier.
items.answer: A) It establishes the setting and a calm, peaceful mood.

steps: An opening stanza often sets up where and when the poem takes place and the mood the reader should feel.
Words like morning light, golden hush, gentle breeze, and dew create a calm, peaceful setting.
A is correct because it names this setting and mood-building job.
B is wrong because there is no conflict or problem stated in these lines.
C is wrong because a turning point comes later, after something has been built up; this is the start.
D is wrong because nothing has been introduced yet for the stanza to resolve.
solution.answer: A) It establishes the setting and a calm, peaceful mood.

items.prompt:
Read this scene from the middle of a story.

For weeks Tessa and her best friend Lin had planned the science fair project together. But in the gym that morning, Tessa saw the poster. Lin's name was on it alone. Her own name was nowhere. Tessa's face went hot. She marched toward Lin, the words already forming in her mouth. They needed to talk, and not quietly.

How does this scene move the plot forward?
A) It resolves the friendship between Tessa and Lin once and for all.
B) It introduces the central conflict between Tessa and Lin that drives the rest of the story.
C) It simply retells that the girls made a science fair project.
D) It establishes the calm, friendly setting of the school.
items.answer: B) It introduces the central conflict between Tessa and Lin that drives the rest of the story.

steps: A scene moves the plot forward by setting up something that the rest of the story will deal with.
Tessa discovers her name is missing from the poster, gets angry, and heads toward Lin to confront her, which creates the conflict that the story will follow.
B is correct because it names that the conflict is being introduced and that it will drive later events.
A is wrong because nothing is resolved; the argument is only beginning.
C is wrong because it only retells events without explaining the structural job the scene does.
D is wrong because the scene is tense and angry, not calm and friendly, and its job is to start a conflict, not establish setting.
solution.answer: B) It introduces the central conflict between Tessa and Lin that drives the rest of the story.

items.prompt:
Read these two stanzas from a poem.

Stanza 1:
The city roared with light and sound,
With honking cars and crowds around,
The speaker laughed, alive and free,
Among the bright and busy sea.

Stanza 2:
But now the streets are dark and bare,
A single lamp, a chill in air,
The speaker walks the road alone,
With only echoes for a home.

How does the second stanza develop the poem?
A) It introduces the main characters of the poem for the first time.
B) It shifts the setting from a bright, busy day to a dark, lonely night to match the speaker's changed feelings.
C) It only repeats the same setting and mood as the first stanza.
D) It resolves the poem by returning the speaker to the happy crowd.
items.answer: B) It shifts the setting from a bright, busy day to a dark, lonely night to match the speaker's changed feelings.

steps: To answer, compare the second stanza to the first and see what changes.

Stanza 1 shows a bright, loud, crowded city where the speaker feels free; stanza 2 shows dark, bare streets where the speaker is alone, so the setting and mood shift from busy and happy to lonely and cold.
B is correct because it names this shift in setting and links it to the speaker's changed feelings.
A is wrong because the speaker is already present in stanza 1, so no one new is introduced.
C is wrong because the mood clearly changes; it does not repeat the first stanza.
D is wrong because the speaker ends up alone, not back in a happy crowd, so nothing is resolved happily.
solution.answer: B) It shifts the setting from a bright, busy day to a dark, lonely night to match the speaker's changed feelings.

items.prompt:
Read this excerpt from the final chapter of a novel.

For a long moment Rosa stared at her younger brother, who had broken her model and then lied about it for days. She had every right to stay angry. But she remembered all the times he had stood by her. Slowly she set down the broken pieces. "It's okay," she said. "You're my brother. That matters more."

Throughout the novel Rosa has struggled with whether to forgive people who hurt her.

How does this ending contribute to the theme of the novel?
A) By showing Rosa choose her brother over her anger, it develops the theme that family bonds matter more than being right.
B) It introduces a new conflict between Rosa and her brother for the next book.
C) It develops the setting by describing the room where Rosa stands.
D) It teaches the generic lesson that lying is always wrong.
items.answer: A) By showing Rosa choose her brother over her anger, it develops the theme that family bonds matter more than being right.

steps: An ending develops the theme by showing how the main struggle of the story is finally resolved and what idea that resolution reveals.
The novel is about whether to forgive, and in the end Rosa forgives her brother because their bond matters more than her anger, which points to the theme that family matters more than being right.
A is correct because it ties the ending to the central idea the whole novel has built.
B is wrong because the ending resolves the conflict rather than starting a new one.
C is wrong because the excerpt focuses on Rosa's choice, not on describing a setting.
D is wrong because it forces a generic moral; the text supports forgiveness and family bonds, not a lesson that lying is always wrong.
solution.answer: A) By showing Rosa choose her brother over her anger, it develops the theme that family bonds matter more than being right.

items.prompt:
Read this passage. It is told in the present, but a memory is placed in the middle.

Daniel held the championship trophy and the crowd cheered, but his hands felt cold. Then the memory came: he was eight years old again, dropping the ball in the final seconds, hearing the groan of the crowd and his coach turning away without a word. Back in the present, the cheering returned. Daniel looked at the trophy and finally let himself smile. The old failure no longer owned him.

Why did the author most likely place the memory of the dropped ball in the middle of this winning moment instead of at the very beginning?
A) The placement is random and could appear anywhere without changing the passage.
B) Placing the failure inside the victory lets the reader feel how Daniel's past loss makes his present win meaningful and shows him moving past it.
C) The memory belongs at the beginning because stories must always be told in order.
D) The memory's only job is to retell what happened when Daniel was eight.
items.answer: B) Placing the failure inside the victory lets the reader feel how Daniel's past loss makes his present win meaningful and shows him moving past it.

steps: This question asks you to judge why the author ordered the parts the way they did and what effect that creates.

By dropping the old failure into the middle of the winning moment, the author lets the reader see the contrast directly, so the present victory feels earned and Daniel's line about the failure no longer owning him shows he has grown.
B is correct because it explains the effect of the placement on the reader's understanding.
A is wrong because the placement is purposeful; moving it would weaken the contrast between past loss and present win.
C is wrong because authors often move events out of order on purpose, like a flashback, for effect.
D is wrong because the memory does more than retell the past; it shapes the meaning of the present scene.
solution.answer: B) Placing the failure inside the victory lets the reader feel how Daniel's past loss makes his present win meaningful and shows him moving past it.

items.prompt:
Read this short poem.

The river runs and will not wait,
It does not pause for love or hate.
We build our walls along the shore,
The river runs, and we are more.

The seasons turn and will not wait,
They do not pause for small or great.
We count our days and lock the door,
The seasons turn, and we are more.

The repeated line "and we are more" closes both stanzas. How does repeating this line at the end of each stanza shape the poem's meaning?
A) The repetition is just filler and adds no meaning to the poem.
B) By ending both stanzas the same way, the repetition ties the river and the seasons together and stresses the theme that people endure and grow even as time keeps moving.
C) The repeated line changes the setting from a river to a city.
D) The repeated line introduces a new character in the second stanza.
items.answer: B) By ending both stanzas the same way, the repetition ties the river and the seasons together and stresses the theme that people endure and grow even as time keeps moving.

steps: A refrain, a line repeated at the end of stanzas, is a structural choice, so the question is what effect that repetition has on meaning.
Both the river and the seasons keep moving and do not wait, yet each stanza ends with "and we are more," which links the two images and emphasizes that people endure and grow as time passes.
B is correct because it explains how the refrain connects the parts and develops the theme.
A is wrong because the repetition is purposeful and carries the poem's main idea.
C is wrong because the setting shifts from a river to the seasons, not to a city, and the refrain itself does not change the setting.
D is wrong because the repeated line introduces no character; it restates the poem's theme.
solution.answer: B) By ending both stanzas the same way, the repetition ties the river and the seasons together and stresses the theme that people endure and grow even as time keeps moving.
